attribution: Traditionally attributed to Vyasa and narrated by his son Shuka; composite authorship
author: vyasa
period: Scholars commonly place its composition between roughly the 6th and 10th centuries CE, often associating it with South India
summary: The most influential Purana of Krishna devotion, telling the stories of Vishnu's descents and above all Krishna's life, with extended philosophical teaching.
whyRead: It is the scriptural heart of many Vaishnava bhakti traditions, and its tenth canto shaped Indian poetry, music, dance and theology. It joins vivid narrative to sustained reflection on devotion, knowledge and grace.
story: The Purana is framed as the sage Shuka narrating to King Parikshit, who has seven days to live. Within this frame come the stories of creation, of Vishnu's descents (avataras) and of devotees, culminating in Krishna's life and teaching.
questions: What is devotion, and can love of God be a path to liberation?
Why does God take form and act in the world?
How do knowledge and devotion relate?

keyTeachings.title: Krishna as the supreme
keyTeachings.text: Among the lists of Vishnu's descents, the text singles out Krishna as the Lord himself rather than a partial descent. This claim is central to many Krishna-centred traditions.

keyTeachings.title: Devotion as the highest aim
keyTeachings.text: Bhakti, devotion that is selfless and uninterrupted, is presented as superior even to liberation sought for oneself. Knowledge and dispassion are said to follow from it.

keyTeachings.title: The devotees' stories
keyTeachings.text: Figures such as Prahlada (canto 7), who remains devoted to Vishnu despite his father's persecution, and Dhruva (canto 4), a child who seeks and finds Vishnu through austerity, serve as models of devotion.

keyTeachings.title: Krishna's life and the gopis
keyTeachings.text: The tenth canto narrates Krishna's childhood and youth in Vraja and his love for the gopis (cowherd women). Their longing is read by many traditions as the highest form of prema, divine love.

keyTeachings.title: Teaching to Uddhava
keyTeachings.text: The eleventh canto contains Krishna's last major teaching, to his friend Uddhava, often called the Uddhava Gita, covering renunciation, knowledge, yoga and devotion.

structure.label: Cantos 1–9
structure.note: Frame story, creation, Kapila's teaching (canto 3), Dhruva (canto 4), Prahlada (canto 7), other descents and dynasties

structure.label: Canto 10

structure.note: The Uddhava Gita and the end of Krishna's earthly presence

structure.note: The age of Kali and the conclusion of the frame story
